category_title: Quiet fourth-grade student with learning disabilities who prefers working alone and struggles with task initiation
student_description: Tyrone is a quiet, independent student who struggles with task initiation, language fluency, and idea generation, often masking his difficulties by sitting silently and claiming he is doing 'Great.' He uniquely requires proactive one-on-one engagement, concrete structural tools (like graphic organizers or cut-and-paste strategies), and multimodal or highly personal prompts to overcome his resistance to writing.

criteria.rationale: Traditional text-only approaches exacerbate Tyrone's language fluency barriers, whereas integrating technology and visuals bypasses this block and excites him.
criteria.check: The long-term plan incorporates digital storytelling, visual materials, or audio elements into his writing assignments.

criteria.rationale: Tyrone needs a predictable, highly structured routine to prevent him from freezing up when faced with a blank page.
criteria.check: The long-term plan establishes a consistent routine that breaks writing into explicit phases (e.g., analyzing the prompt, planning with a graphic organizer, drafting, and revising based on feedback).

criteria.rationale: Relentless, generalized drilling increases Tyrone's stress, whereas targeted, one-on-one feedback helps him make steady progress.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes dedicated time for one-on-one conferencing or providing specific, individualized comments to guide his revisions, explicitly avoiding generic or relentless drilling.
